payload.title: Same-Sex Marriage in Greece and What Couples Need
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian same-sex couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more who have set their hearts on a wedding in Greece and want to know, before they book a venue or tell their guests, whether they can legally marry there as visitors, which documents Australians need, whether the marriage is recognised back home, what kind of ceremony is open to them, and how to choose an island and venue that genuinely welcomes them, so they can plan with confidence and then hand the celebration to someone who will look after it.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation at /wonderland-concierge so an advisor can plan the venue, travel, vendors and guest stays around the ceremony (the legal paperwork stays with the couple, the municipality and the authorities).
payload.angle: Most page-one results for 'same sex marriage greece' are news reports on the law change or generic all-countries lists, and few answer the practical question an Australian couple has: can we, as visitors, actually marry in Greece, and what do we need. This guide states the legal position only from official sources read live and dates it once (as at November 2026): what the law allows, since when, and that it is civil marriage. It then walks Australians through the visitor steps, documents (Certificate of No Impediment, translation, Apostille, the Australian Embassy in Athens) and recognition back home exactly as the official pages state them, separates civil, symbolic and religious ceremonies plainly, and gives a short list of questions to ask an island venue, naming venues only where their own site says they welcome same-sex or LGBTQ+ weddings. Travel advice is Smartraveller's LGBTI guidance as worded. Respectful, plain and practical, with no politics.
must_include: Intro with a direct answer in the first 100 words: the legal position as an official source states it, dated 'as at November 2026', that it is a civil marriage, and that visitors should check the steps with the municipality and the Australian Embassy in Athens before booking. Link /expert-advice/where-can-same-sex-couples-legally-marry-abroad here (anchor about where same-sex couples can legally marry abroad).

Exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways (the law and that it is civil marriage; visitors and the municipality steps as sourced; Australian documents and recognition; choose a venue that says it welcomes same-sex or LGBTQ+ weddings).

Is same-sex marriage legal in Greece: the law, the date it took effect and that marriage is civil, stated only from an official Greek government or Australian government source read live; dated once as at November 2026. No adoption, parenthood or civil partnership detail unless an official source supports it, and then only one line.

Can visitors marry there: residency requirement (or none), documents and municipality steps exactly as an official source states them; where a step, timeframe or fee is not stated, write 'check with the municipality and the embassy, including any fees'.

Documents for Australians: Certificate of No Impediment, translation into Greek, Apostille and the Australian Embassy in Athens, only as Smartraveller, DFAT or the Embassy state them, as at November 2026.
Recognition back home: how an overseas marriage is treated in Australia, from an official Australian source only (no legal advice; 'check with the authorities').

Civil, symbolic or religious: civil is the legal route; a symbolic ceremony can follow at a venue; the Orthodox Church marries a man and a woman, stated plainly from the church or official source with no religious commentary. Link /destination-weddings/greek-orthodox-wedding.

Choosing an island and venue: questions to ask (do you host same-sex or LGBTQ+ weddings, can the civil ceremony and celebration be on the same day, who the officiant is, privacy, guest stays); venues named only where their own site says they welcome same-sex or LGBTQ+ weddings; links /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding, /destination-weddings/mykonos-wedding, /destination-weddings/rhodes-wedding-venues, /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues. This section carries the ONLY Advisor line in the body (brand-facts claims only, framed around venue, travel, vendors and guests, never paperwork), plus a link to /wonderland-concierge.
Travel advice: Smartraveller's LGBTI guidance for Greece as worded, short and factual.

FAQ (4 to 6): Is same-sex marriage legal in Greece? Can Australians marry in Greece without living there? What documents do Australians need? Is a Greek same-sex marriage recognised in Australia? Can we have a church wedding in Greece? Each answer from the same sources as the body.

Close: the one Advisor line from brand-facts.md (never the definition line or its closing phrase). Links: /expert-advice/where-can-same-sex-couples-legally-marry-abroad (both ways), /wonderland-concierge (anchor names 'Wedded Concierge'), /magazine as the magnet. UTMs utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=same-sex-marriage-greece&utm_content=primary|secondary|magnet|closing on /wonderland-concierge and /magazine only.
avoid: Any legal statement not from an official source read live; undated legal claims; legal advice.
Adoption, parenthood or civil partnership detail unless an official source supports it.
Politics, opinion on the law, its passage or opponents; religious commentary; stereotypes; 'brave', 'finally' or celebratory framing of the law.
Any price, fee or amount; 'free'; transfers, drive or flight times.
Naming a venue as welcoming unless its own site says it welcomes same-sex or LGBTQ+ weddings; venue contact or business details; vendor names.
Anything that implies the Wedded Advisor or Wedded Concierge helps with legal paperwork, documents, the municipality or the embassy.
Research talk in copy ('we could not confirm', 'on its own site'); per-line source credits; hedge stacking.
Competitor wedding sites, directories, planner blogs, news opinion or Wikipedia as sources; competitor wording or images.

Wedded Privileges; Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; more than one Advisor line in the body besides the close; the Advisor definition line and the phrase 'last dance'; 'Wonderland Concierge' as anchor text.
Clichés (fairytale, dream day, breathtaking), exclamation marks, keywords pasted in headings, em dashes, US spelling.
AI images of any venue, destination or wedding; stock imagery that stereotypes couples.
